title: Speaking: special dates and using a calendar
competency: Talk about a special date and about the Ethiopian and Gregorian calendars.

keywords.def: A year with one extra day, every four years.

ideas.name: Months, new years and using a calendar

en.text: The Ethiopian New Year is Meskerem 1; the Gregorian New Year is January 1. A rhyme helps you remember the Gregorian months: September, April, June and November have 30 days; February has 28, or 29 in a leap year; the rest have 31. On a calendar, red dates are holidays and black dates are working days.

am.text: የኢትዮጵያ አዲስ ዓመት መስከረም 1፣ የፈረንጆች ደግሞ ጃንዩዌሪ 1 ነው። በቀን መቁጠሪያ ቀይ ቀናት በዓላት፣ ጥቁሮቹ የሥራ ቀናት ናቸው።

screens.title: Two pictures
screens.ask: Picture A shows መስከረም ፩. Picture B shows "1 JANUARY". What do both pictures show?
screens.after: Meskerem 1 is the Ethiopian New Year; January 1 is the Gregorian New Year.

screens.title: Using a calendar
paras: Student: Sir, would you please tell me how to use a calendar?
Teacher: Of course. Look at the calendar. What do you see?
Student: Names of months and days.
Student: There are dates also. Some are in black colour and some others are in red colour.
Teacher: The dates and days tell you what date each day is.
Teacher: The red colours are holidays, but the black ones show working days.

screens.title: Key words
defs: A year with one extra day, every four years.
A day when people do not work, often shown in red on a calendar.

screens.text: Activity 2.9 d: which months have 30 days?
screens.why: "Thirty days has September, April, June and November."

screens.text: Activity 2.9 b: which month has 28 days (29 in a leap year)?
Activity 2.9 a: what type of calendar is the poem about?
screens.why: It names Gregorian months and the leap year.

screens.text: In the dialogue, black dates on a calendar are holidays.
screens.why: "The red colours are holidays, but the black ones show working days."
screens.clue: What did the teacher say about red?

screens.text: Using the poem, how many days are there in July and August together?
screens.why: Neither month is in the 30-day list or February, so both have 31 days: 31 + 31 = 62.
screens.clue: Is July in the "thirty days" list?
